findings.title: STRICT design review plan omits required verifier invocation details
findings.problem: The design document does not fully specify the independent verifier invocation contract required for a STRICT change.
findings.description: The schema requires each independent verification step to document the built-in subagent API, `fork_context=false`, and template `verify-reviewer-inline-v3`. The current design review-plan section documents the sequence, contracts, agent path, lifecycle, and output paths, but it does not state the built-in subagent invocation rule or `fork_context=false`.
findings.evidence: Schema requirement: `openspec/schemas/ai-enforced-workflow/schema.yaml:158-172` requires design.md to document `invocation: built-in subagent API, fork_context=false, template verify-reviewer-inline-v3`. Current design coverage: `openspec/changes/restructure-steering-domain-architecture/design.md:300-378` documents sequence, contracts, agent path, lifecycle, and output paths, but there is no explicit `fork_context=false` or built-in subagent API statement. Repo search over the reviewed change docs returned no matches for `fork_context` or `built-in subagent`.
findings.recommendation: Amend `design.md` so the docs-first and source-first checkpoint plan explicitly states that verifier review is invoked through the built-in subagent API with `fork_context=false` and template `verify-reviewer-inline-v3`, matching the schema wording.

findings.title: STRICT review tasks do not require subject binding or finding-routing semantics
findings.problem: The task plan does not carry all verification-contract requirements that the schema mandates for STANDARD/STRICT review tasks.
findings.description: The schema requires verification tasks to reference `subject_required_any_of` and the findings-routing field groups (`findings_required`, `finding_object_required`, `finding_semantics`, `repair_routing_rules`) in addition to the shared field groups and output paths. The current tasks document references the sequence, contracts, lifecycle, routing target, output paths, and `agent-table.json`, but it never requires subject binding or the findings-routing semantics.
findings.evidence: Schema requirement: `openspec/schemas/ai-enforced-workflow/schema.yaml:211-221` requires STANDARD/STRICT verification tasks to require execution evidence using `verifier_evidence_required`, require subject binding through `subject_required_any_of`, and carry findings-routing semantics from `findings_required / finding_object_required / finding_semantics / repair_routing_rules`. The current task contract and checkpoint tasks at `openspec/changes/restructure-steering-domain-architecture/tasks.md:1-23`, `:33`, and `:118-119` do not mention those items. The shared contract does define them at `openspec/schemas/modules/verification-cycle/contracts/verification-cycle-core-v1.json:84-141`.
findings.recommendation: Update the verification contract preamble and both checkpoint tasks in `tasks.md` to explicitly require subject binding through `subject_required_any_of` and the findings-routing semantics from the shared core contract, not just the field-group list and output paths.

findings.title: Transport is declared in the dependency scan scope but excluded from the actual runtime-dependency guard
findings.problem: The dependency-direction requirement and task-level verification leave `transport/` outside the explicit no-`runtime/*` enforcement, even though `transport/` is one of the new top-level domain layers and the design argues it should be separate from runtime.
findings.description: The spec says dependency checks scan `new/code/transport`, but the normative THEN clause only forbids `runtime/*` includes for `vision`, `reference`, `control`, `safety`, and `observability`. The task-level dependency check similarly omits `new/code/transport`. That mismatch leaves one of the target layers without an explicit dependency-direction gate.
findings.evidence: Spec mismatch: `openspec/changes/restructure-steering-domain-architecture/specs/steering-domain-architecture/spec.md:16-22` says the scan covers `new/code/transport` but only forbids `runtime/*` headers for `vision`, `reference`, `control`, `safety`, and `observability`. Task-level check: `openspec/changes/restructure-steering-domain-architecture/tasks.md:72` scans only `new/code/reference new/code/control new/code/safety new/code/observability new/code/vision`. Design intent still separates transport from runtime at `openspec/changes/restructure-steering-domain-architecture/design.md:223-251`.
findings.recommendation: Make the dependency rule and task checks consistent: either explicitly forbid `transport/` from including `runtime/*` like the other domain layers, or document a narrow allowed exception with a follow-up task and dedicated verification gate.

findings.title: Final validation task uses an unsupported `openspec validate` flag
findings.problem: One of the planned verification commands cannot run as written.
findings.description: Task 10.2 uses `rtk openspec validate --change restructure-steering-domain-architecture`, but the installed CLI does not support a `--change` flag for `openspec validate`. That means the documented final verification step is currently non-executable.
findings.evidence: Task text: `openspec/changes/restructure-steering-domain-architecture/tasks.md:117` uses `rtk openspec validate --change restructure-steering-domain-architecture`. Running that command returned exit code 1 with `error: unknown option '--change'`. `openspec validate --help` shows supported forms are `openspec validate [item-name]`, `--all`, `--changes`, `--specs`, and `--type <type>`.
findings.recommendation: Replace task 10.2 with a supported command such as `rtk openspec validate restructure-steering-domain-architecture --type change` or another repo-approved equivalent, then keep the final verification flow aligned with the actual CLI.
